entries.title: Acronyms and Four Principles of Family Medicine

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Professional - Accountability to patients and their families
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The CFPC's Four Principles of Family Medicine (expert generalist care of undifferentiated disease; community-based/adaptive practice; resource to a defined practice population; centrality of the patient-physician relationship) articulate the professional-identity and continuity-of-care commitments that MCC's Professional role role-level statement captures generically ('Provide care that meets or exceeds expected standards of competence'; 'Ensure continuity of care'). No Medical Expert presentation-level objective exists for this foundational-philosophy content, so role-level evidence is used rather than fabricating a disease-specific MCC ID.

testable_competencies.professional_identity: Recognize the CFPC's four principles of family medicine (expert generalist care of undifferentiated disease; community-based/adaptive practice; resource to a defined practice population; centrality of the patient-physician relationship) as the professional-identity framework underlying primary care.

entries.zero_question_reason: Glossary and professional-identity/philosophy framing content; not an independently testable clinical competency, retained as context for the rest of the chapter.
entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: Role-level Professional evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because it is the only available canonical anchor for the Four Principles of Family Medicine content and directly informs this unit's CONTEXT_ONLY scope depth; omitting it would leave the professional-identity framing entirely untraceable to any MCC source.

entries.title: Purpose of the Periodic Health Examination and Classification of Recommendations (GRADE)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74 ('the candidate will assess age- and sex-specific risk factors to guide the history, physical examination, screening investigations, and counselling') presumes the candidate understands the purpose/structure of a periodic health encounter and how evidence is graded; this unit is the methodological scaffolding component of that objective rather than a standalone testable presentation.

testable_competencies.phe_framework: Explain the purpose of the periodic health examination and interpret GRADE-style strength-of-recommendation/quality-of-evidence labels attached to screening guidelines.

entries.zero_question_reason: Framework/methodology content underlying the screening-guideline units that follow; not independently testable as its own clinical scenario.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74 explicitly names 'screening investigations' guided by age- and sex-specific risk factors as core Medical Expert content; targeted registry search found no dedicated per-cancer screening-program objective (queried 'cancer', 'screening', and the specific cancer site), so objective 74 is the direct evidence for breast cancer screening.

testable_competencies.screening_recommendations: Apply current periodic-health-examination screening recommendations for breast cancer screening to a given patient's age/sex/risk profile, including when to start, stop, and how to interpret an abnormal result.

entries.title: Osteoporosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No dedicated MCC osteoporosis objective exists (targeted registry search for 'osteoporosis'/'bone density'/'fracture' returned no direct match beyond bone/joint injury); TN frames osteoporosis primarily as an age/sex-based periodic-health-examination screening topic (bone mineral density testing), mapped as a component of objective 74.

testable_competencies.osteoporosis: Apply bone-mineral-density screening criteria for osteoporosis and initiate first-line management (calcium/vitamin D, bisphosphonates) based on fracture-risk assessment.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with Calcium disorders (objective 12-2, used by Endocrinology chapter E for metabolic bone disease, SU-E-48 through SU-E-51) - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Rash

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38 (Skin and integument conditions) is the MCC presentation-level objective covering rash; located via targeted registry search ('skin lesion') after 'rash'/'dermatitis' returned no direct title match.

testable_competencies.rash: Diagnose common primary-care rash presentations and differentiate benign from urgent/serious causes.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with Dermatology (chapter D, completed), which covers skin/integument conditions in full diagnostic/morphologic detail against the same objective. FM's content is the primary-care undifferentiated-rash-triage angle - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for STIs generally (targeted registry search for 'sexually transmitted'/'chlamydia'/'urethritis'/'genital ulcer' returned no direct match); the closest available presentation-level objective, vaginal discharge/vulvar pruritus, covers only the female-presentation component of the TN STI subsection, so this is mapped as COMPONENT/MODERATE with the acknowledged gap for male-presentation (urethral discharge) and asymptomatic-screening content.

testable_competencies.sti: Diagnose and manage common sexually transmitted infections (chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, HPV, HSV) in a primary-care patient, including partner notification and safer-sex counselling.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with Gynecology (chapter GY), Urology (chapter U), and Infectious Diseases (chapter ID, all not yet mapped) - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No dedicated MCC sinusitis objective exists (targeted registry search for 'sinusitis'/'sinus'/'rhinosinusitis' returned no direct match); sinusitis is a cause of rhinorrhea (and overlaps with headache/facial-pain presentations), mapped as a component of objective 100.

testable_competencies.sinusitis: Diagnose acute bacterial vs. viral rhinosinusitis using duration/severity criteria and initiate appropriate management, avoiding unnecessary antibiotics.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct presentation-level match to objective 98.

testable_competencies.sleep_disorders: Diagnose common primary-care sleep disorders (e.g., insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea) and initiate an appropriate management plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct presentation-level match to objective 100.

testable_competencies.pharyngitis: Diagnose the cause of sore throat/pharyngitis, apply criteria (e.g., Centor score) to identify likely streptococcal pharyngitis, and initiate appropriate management.

entries.title: Principles of Palliative Care and End-of-Life Care Discussions

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No Medical Expert presentation-level MCC objective exists for 'palliative care' as a topic (targeted registry search for 'palliative'/'end of life'/'goals of care' returned no direct match); the early-identification, multidisciplinary, and goals-of-care-discussion content described in this TN subsection is core Communicator-role competency (structuring a difficult end-of-life conversation), used here as role-level evidence.

testable_competencies.palliative_principles: Identify patients who could benefit from a palliative approach to care and structure a goals-of-care/end-of-life discussion addressing physical, psychological, social, and spiritual needs.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Palliative Medicine (chapter PM, not yet mapped) will cover this in full specialist detail; ELOM (chapter ELOM, completed) already covers end-of-life/goals-of-care communication and consent principles from the ethical/legal angle. FM's content is the primary-care early-identification and initial-conversation angle - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Power of Attorney and Instructional Advance Directives

testable_competencies.advance_care_planning: Explain the distinction between a Power of Attorney for personal care (substitute decision-maker) and an instructional advance directive, and counsel a patient on advance care planning.

entries.zero_question_reason: Purely legal/jurisdictional documentation content; substantive ethical-legal framework and jurisdiction-specific consent hierarchy already belongs to ELOM (chapter ELOM, completed), which covers substitute decision-making and advance directives from the canonical ethics/law angle. This FM subsection duplicates that framework applied to the palliative-care context without adding a distinct testable competency.
entries.cross_discipline_note: ELOM (chapter ELOM, completed) is the primary owner of Power of Attorney / advance-directive / substitute-decision-maker content; this FM subsection is a thin duplicate applied to the palliative context. Classified CROSS_DISCIPLINE rather than DIRECT/COMPONENT - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit (candidate for CROSS_LINK at global-audit stage).

entries.title: Symptom Management in Palliative Care

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Medical Expert - symptom management in a palliative approach to care
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No single MCC presentation-level objective covers 'palliative symptom management' as a topic; the underlying symptoms (pain, dyspnea, nausea) are individually covered by other Medical Expert objectives (e.g., Generalized pain disorders, Dyspnea) but the TN content here is specifically their palliative-intent management, which is best represented as role-level Medical Expert context pending a dedicated objective search once Palliative Medicine (chapter PM) is mapped.

testable_competencies.symptom_management: Select appropriate pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic management for common palliative-care symptoms (pain, dyspnea, nausea, delirium) with palliative intent.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Palliative Medicine (chapter PM, not yet mapped) will own this content in full specialist detail - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Complementary and Integrative Medicine (Common Herbal Products)

testable_competencies.herbal_product_safety: Recognize reported uses, possible adverse effects, and possible drug interactions of common herbal/natural health products a patient may disclose using.

entries.zero_question_reason: Reference table of herbal-product facts; no MCC presentation-level objective matches this content and it is background/reference rather than an independently testable clinical scenario.

entries.title: Antimicrobial/Antiviral/Antifungal Quick Reference
entries.zero_question_reason: Cross-condition empiric-therapy quick-reference table duplicating management content already represented within each individual presenting-problem unit above (e.g., Sore Throat/Pharyngitis, Sinusitis, Common Cold); retained for source-node traceability only, not an independent testable unit.

entries.title: Landmark Family Medicine Trials and References
entries.zero_question_reason: Bibliographic trial-summary table and chapter references appendix; source-attribution content, not an independently testable clinical competency.
